Done. Changes:

**`src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__widen_idempotency_key.sql`** (new) — `ALTER TABLE payment ALTER COLUMN idempotency_key TYPE VARCHAR(128);`

I left `V1__init.sql` at `VARCHAR(64)` rather than editing it in place: Flyway checksums applied migrations, so rewriting V1 would break startup on any database that already ran it, and it wouldn't widen an existing column anyway. A forward migration widens both existing and fresh databases.

Nothing else constrains the length — I checked all of it:
- `Payment.java:14` — `@Column(nullable = false)` with no `length`, so the mapping was never pinned to 64 (Hibernate's default is 255). Left as-is; adding `length = 128` would introduce a constraint rather than widen one, so say the word if you'd rather have the entity mirror the schema explicitly.
- `PaymentValidator.check` only rejects null/blank keys, no length check.
- `payment.graphqls:12` and `PaymentDto` use plain `String` — unbounded.

Two things to confirm on your side:
- The `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE` syntax is PostgreSQL/H2. If this runs against MySQL it needs `MODIFY idempotency_key VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL`. There's no `application.properties` in the repo, so I couldn't determine the target database.
- `pom.xml` has no Flyway dependency, only `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa`, so nothing on the classpath currently executes `db/migration` — the migrations appear to be applied by something outside this module.
